name: Portland Douglas-fir plywood panels
description: Portland Manufacturing produced three-ply Douglas-fir panels displayed at the 1905 Portland exposition.

date.basis: Date for the cited specific instance, not an invention or global priority date.

events.statement: Portland Manufacturing produced three-ply Douglas-fir panels displayed at the 1905 Portland exposition.

evidence.supports: The Oregon Historical Society describes the display and promotion to door and cabinet makers.
The retrospective identifies veneer cut on a lathe for the 1905 panels.

The National Register nomination states that a rotary veneer plant began operating at Portland Manufacturing in early 1902, and that the firm experimented with panels of rotary-cut Douglas-fir veneers in 1904 before their 1905 exposition display. Its history cites Thomas Autzen’s 1953 company account. This supports a rotary-cut veneer prerequisite without proving that the 1905 exposition introduced plywood globally.

events.caveats: Plywood and veneer existed earlier; this exhibit does not prove a world first or the date of widespread structural use.
